entry.title: Focaccia
entry.content:
1. In a big bowl, combine flour + yeast.
  2. Add water, mix with a spoon until flour is worked in
  3. Add salt and olive oil, and gently mix in (it will be goopy). Let it rest for 15 mins
  4. Do 4 sets of coil folds every 25 minutes
  5. With wet hands, lift one side of the dough, let it stretch and fold it under itself. Rotate and repeat on all sides. Cover with damp towel between sets
  6. Cover the bowl tightly and refrigerate for 12-48hrs. It should rise a bit and be full of bubbles. 24 hours is a good amount of time
  7. Generously oil your pan (don’t skimp, at least 2-3tbsp)
  8. Gently pour the cold dough into the pan. Don’t deflate it. Add a drizzle of olive oil on top.
  9. Let it proof at room temp for 4-5hrs until it’s puffy and bubbly
  10. Preheat oven to 232℃
  11. With oiled fingers, dimple the dough. Top with flaky salt, rosemary, garlic.
  12. Drizzle more olive oil on top to help crisp the surface
  13. Bake for 20-25mins until deeply golden and crisp
  14. Cool in pan for at least 10min before removing

entry.title: Salt Bread
entry.content:
1. In the mixing bowl, add all the ingredients and mix with a dough hook for 10 mins until the dough comes together (dough will be sticky).
  2. Remove the dough from mixer and slap and fold until it comes together (~3-5mins), cover and rest for 15min .
  3. 1st stretch and fold on all 4 sides, cover and rest for 15min
  4. 2nd stretch and fold on all 4 sides
  5. Rest until the dough doubles in size (~1.5h)
  6. After 1.5h of bulk proofing, using a scale, cut and measure 80g balls of dough
  7. Roll each ball and tuck in the bottom (stretch the skin)
  8. Place on baking paper on a tray, cover and rest until it doubles in size (~30mins)
  9. Cut the butter up into 10-12g blocks and freeze before use
  10. Take the ball of dough and roll it into a log. Roll down once with the rolling pin (thin) and roll up (increasing width toward the top), place the butter block at the top, and roll the butter in the centre of the roll.
  11. Preheat the oven to 200c, no fan
  12. Rest until the rolls double in size again (~30min)
  13. Spray the rolls with water and top with flaky salt
  14. Bake the bread rolls for 20mins at 200c.
  15. Melt salted butter ~3mins before the bread is ready to come out of the oven
  16. Once the bread is out, immediately brush the rolls with melted butter.
  17. Allow to cool, serve and enjoy.

Tips: ⁠ ⁠When removing dough from mixer after the first 10min mixer-knead, wet your hands to prevent sticking Remember to flour your working surface when kneading, cutting and rolling to prevent sticking ⁠⁠If the dough is too sticky, add bread flour bit by bit, if it is too dry, more water on your hands should do the trick

entry.title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
entry.content:
1. In a large bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda, cornstarch, and salt together. Set aside.
  2. In a medium bowl, whisk the melted butter, brown sugar, and caster sugar together until no lumps remain. Whisk in the egg and egg yolk until combined, then whisk in the vanilla extract. Pour into dry ingredients and mix together with a large spoon or spatula. Fold in the chocolate chips.
  3. Cover the dough tightly and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or up to 3 days.
  4. Preheat oven to 163°C. Line large baking sheets with parchment paper.
  5. Add chocolate chips to the top and flaky sea salt (optional).
  6. Bake cookies for a total of 13 minutes — 7 minutes, remove to round, then bake for another 6 minutes.
  7. Cool on baking sheet for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack.
